analysis:
Both units are BASE excerpts (lines 485-949) of docs/reference/configuration.md. The PR is documentation-only: it bumps the "Last updated" date and rewrites the "Cluster runtime facts" section (around base lines 923-949). The new text says a signed release can register `cluster_runtime` in its POST /v1/releases payload, and that a coordinator accepting it derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it.

The visible base excerpt shows no runtime code or default changes. The prefix-cache, SSD cache, memory and media-budget tables are unchanged context, so T-041 and the SSD cache mitigations are not affected by the changed ranges.

The only security-relevant part is the new description of release-derived trust. It touches A-005 (release API key), A-011 (binary hash registry) and A-017 (durable build qualifications). Previously a human operator copied the digests into an approval file. Under the new flow, a release registration can auto-derive pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. That authority is platform-owned: the coordinator is out of scope, and the evidence supplied here is a truncated patch excerpt and the BASE text only.

I could not verify whether the coordinator gates this derivation on the A-005 key, on an independent qualification step (A-017), or on the environment variable. The head text is not supplied, so the exact new wording is unseen.

I report no finding, since a documentation claim about an external implementation is not evidence of a regression. Integration should check that the docs do not imply release publication alone confers serving authorization. That would be inconsistent with A-017, which says release publication is distinct from qualification, and with T-052 and T-054.

The docs/operations/provider-release.md anchor and the platform-side implementation were not supplied.
